items.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
items.summary: Streaming video understanding requires models to repeatedly decide whether to respond or continue observing. Recently, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been applied to this setting, with existing approaches emphasizing reward design while retaining a single trajectory-level advantage across turns. Such shared credit can reinforce redundant replies after earlier successes and discourage useful follow-ups after earlier failures. items.title: LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers
items.summary: Looped transformers are a parameter-efficient alternative to standard transformers for language modeling. By reapplying the same layers across multiple loop steps, recent looped language models match the performance of non-looped models several times their size. While this architecture effectively reduces parameter memory, each loop step still stores its own keys and values, so the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with the number of loop steps and becomes the main memory bottleneck. items.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target. items.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
items.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) extends on-policy distillation (OPD) to consolidate capabilities from multiple teachers. Although prior work reports near-perfect in-distribution (IND) distillation performance, we find that this can mask incomplete capability consolidation beyond the supervised distribution. A preliminary study on synthetic reasoning shows that OPD does not fully transfer teachers' generalization capabilities. items.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
items.summary: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. Sustaining such a dialogue requires more than answering each question in isolation: the model must retrieve and reuse information established earlier in the conversation, both what it has seen and what it has said, an ability we term in-context video memory. items.summary: Few-step distillation offers efficient generation with diffusion and flow models, but preserving quality with only a few sampling steps remains challenging. Distribution-matching methods via score distillation provide a strong foundation, yet they rely on accurately tracking the student's changing distribution. items.summary: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. items.title: AnchorComplete: Recovering Complete Scene Meshes from Partial Point Clouds
items.summary: Most image-based 3D reconstructors primarily recover visible surfaces, producing partial point clouds with large holes and leaving unobserved geometry unresolved. To address this limitation, we introduce AnchorComplete, a framework that reconstructs complete scene meshes from partial point clouds while preserving observed geometry and supporting scenes of varying scales. items.summary: Vision-language-action models are typically built on a simple premise: perception is first compressed by visual encoders, and action reasoning begins only afterwards. items.summary: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. items.summary: Safety alignment for Large Language Models is heavily focused on English with limited multilingual representation, particularly damaging low-resource language performance. Related open training datasets are often limited in size or do not follow region-localized harmful topics to broaden the scope of alignment beyond cultures. items.summary: Teleoperation remains the default way to collect robot demonstrations, but every episode costs robot and operator time, and every new task starts from scratch. We ask whether a coding agent can take over the teleoperator's job. In our DataFarm, the agent receives a data request and one calibration episode of the robot in the target scene and rebuilds the task in simulation: it writes the scene, an expert controller, and a success judge. items.title: Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver
items.summary: Classical structure-from-motion reconstruction proceeds iteratively, refining camera poses and scene geometry from a current estimate. This allows maps to easily expand without recomputing already computed views, or geometry estimates to improve as more observations are provided. Most geometric foundation models, however, predict entire geometry in a single forward pass or update a recurrent state as frames arrive sequentially, making this expansion and refinement non-trivial. items.summary: Speculative decoding (SD) accelerates large language model inference by reducing the sequential cost of token-by-token generation. Advanced SD methods reduce proposal cost with parallel drafters that predict entire blocks in one forward pass, but overall speedup still depends on acceptance length. items.title: VeriSpoof: Beyond Real or Fake with One Audio LLM
items.summary: A speech deepfake detector estimates whether a recording is synthetic, but a forensic analyst also asks which system produced it, whether recordings share a source, and what evidence supports each conclusion. We present VeriSpoof, an audio language model that unifies five tasks with shared weights: deepfake detection, generator attribution (generator, acoustic model and vocoder), recording-condition analysis, synthesized-span localisation, and source verification. items.summary: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. items.title: GameVerse: A Minute-Scale Gameplay Dataset for Long-Horizon Interactive World Modeling
items.summary: Recent advances in interactive world models have made it possible to generate controllable, dynamic environments from action inputs. Yet current models struggle to maintain coherence beyond roughly one minute of rollout, a limitation rooted not in model capacity but in the scarcity of long-horizon training data. Existing gameplay video datasets typically consist of clips under ten seconds, with captions that describe whole clips in coarse and undifferentiated text, which is insufficient for controllable long-horizon generation. items.title: FinForesight: A Diagnostic Backtesting Benchmark for Deep Research Systems in Financial Forecasting
items.summary: Anticipating financial outcomes requires synthesizing evolving evidence and reasoning under uncertainty, making deep research systems promising tools for forecasting. Yet evaluating forecasting ability is challenging because historical backtests may reward memorized outcomes or information retrieved after the forecast date. items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for training multimodal agents to reason and use tools. items.title: 我觉得 ai 时代对于普通人是利好啊，为啥如此多的人反感/不屑呢？
items.summary: 最近逛论坛、看国外的一些文章，发现好多人（包括我常看的一些专栏作者）都对 ai 有不少负面情绪，或者对那种“vibe coding”挺反感的。他们的理由听起来也五花八门的，比如觉得 ai 剥夺了自己亲手敲代码的乐趣啦、担心 ai 巨头变成了垄断生产资料的地主啦、或者觉得人类的价值被贬值等等。 虽说我也能理解这些焦虑，但说实话，要是现在问我“愿不愿意回到没有 ai 的日子”，我绝对会说：打死都不回去，完全回不去了！因为跟现在一比，以前那日子简直就是地狱好吗？ 大家想想过去咱们过的是啥日子。就拿我自己来说吧，上大学那会儿，身边连个 ai 帮手都没有。遇到做不出的数学题、编程题，就硬生生卡在那儿，一点脾气都没有。然后就是无数个熬夜拖延的晚上，眼看着马上要到截止日期了，心里那种焦虑、害怕，好几次甚至直接 ptsd 。再想想初中、高中，那时更没有 ai ，互联网也不像现在这么发达，就算可以网上搜题的答案，家里也不让上网，所以为了应试，只能花冤枉钱去报各种补习班，活生生被当成韭菜割，不知道被收割了多少钱了。 等到了找工作的时候，那就更让人窒息了。你得死记硬背一大堆概念，什么闭包啊、use effect 啊，说句掏心窝子的话，那些概念我到现在都没弄明白。你跟面试官说你会主流的前端框架像 react ，人家觉得你会得不够多，还得精通 html 、css ，你懂了这些，人家又挑刺说你最好还得会 we…

items.title: [送兑换码] 做了个 iOS 翻译 App，用自己的 API Key，多个大模型译文并排对比，送 30 个永久解锁码
items.summary: 平时翻译我习惯同一段话丢给好几个模型，DeepSeek 一份、Claude 一份、Gemini 一份，再挑读起来最顺的那句。来回切 App 、复制粘贴实在太烦，于是做了 **Transory**： - **多模型并排对比**：一次请求多个服务，每个模型一张卡片，流式输出。支持 DeepSeek 、Claude 、Gemini 、OpenAI 、OpenRouter 、硅基流动、Kimi 、智谱、通义千问，以及任何 OpenAI / Anthropic 兼容接口 - **局域网本地模型**：可以连电脑上的 Ollama 、LM Studio - **拍照翻译**：文字在本机用 Vision 识别，译文直接盖在原图对应位置，也能切成对照模式 - **四种风格**：自然 / 正式 / 口语 / 直译；原文已经是目标语言时自动改译成英文 - **隐私**：没有服务器、没有账号、不收集数据。原文只直接发给你自己授权的服务，可以打开「每次发送前确认」。API Key 存在系统钥匙串 ![多模型对比]( https://maple-dawn.github.io/Transory/ios/screenshots/01-translate.jpg) ![拍照翻译]( https://maple-dawn.github.io/Transory/ios/screenshots/02-camera.jpg…
